newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria ups reward for information on bombers.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria ups reward for information on bombers.

text.p: Nigeria on Wednesday offered to pay four million naira ($47,000) to anyone giving information leading to the arrest of perpetrators of a bombing campaign in the country.

Zakari Biu, head of a special police anti-terrorism unit investigating the bombings, said in Lagos that a decision to raise the financial reward for the information from one million naira was part of a re-doubling of efforts to end the bombings.
The latest of such blasts hit a mosque in the eastern city of Onitsha two weeks ago killing five people. Until then the targets had been military vehicles.
"This change of targets from military vehicles to places of worship is intended to provoke ethnic and religious conflicts in the country," Biu said.
Twelve opposition activists including exiled Nobel prize laureate Wole Soyinka have been charged with treason in a Lagos magistrate court over the bombings.
Their pleas are yet to be taken but the opposition NADECO which is blamed by police for the blasts denies any involvement.
Biu said efforts by his unit to extend its investigations of the blasts to Britain, the United States and Spain had so far not been successful because they had not been given visas.
Nigeria's relations with the West are strained over alleged human rights violations by the military government and the slow pace of democratisation of Africa's most populous nation.
